I am old now, 78 years, and my body is tired. This small plot near the house I keep for cassava and a little cowpea mixed together, the way my mother taught me. I have no money for the shop fertilizers, and here in Mtwara the rains come when they come — I cannot carry water to the plot. My children and grandchildren help me with the hoe when they can, but mostly it is me working slowly, small-small.
